findings.issue: The entry states 'Expressed genome-scale CRISPRi perturbation in undifferentiated KOLF2.1J iPSCs, covering 11,739 targeted genes rather than a sampled subset' with is_sample: false. The bundle's October 2025 per-file description states the atlas maps 'transcriptional and fitness phenotypes associated with 11,739 targeted genes' — a targeted gene set, which the project portal calls 'whole-genome'. The is_sample: false assertion is an interpretation of 'genome-scale' rather than a stated fact; the accompanying source_caveats partially discloses this but the boolean itself is not directly attested.

The second strategy cites 'Perturb-seq of 200 genes in the triple-negative breast cancer cell line and immunofluorescence imaging of 523 proteins' from the CM4AI project portal's flagship-dataset panel. Those figures describe the project's TNBC curated dataset generally, not necessarily the contents of this June 2026 release, whose file listing carries no protein or gene counts. The portal figure of 523 proteins also conflicts with the 464-protein figure the October 2025 release gives for the same-named IF archives; this conflict is disclosed for file_collections but not here.

The Ravitsky entry omits `affiliation` while the parallel Bélisle-Pipon entry populates it. The bundle attests 'Ravitsky V (University of Montreal)' in the author list of the same release record from which the ORCID was taken, and the source_caveats already discusses the affiliation/email-domain mismatch, so the affiliation is supported and its omission is an inconsistency between two structurally parallel entries.

The sentence 'these are project-level totals across all CM4AI data streams and are not counts for this release alone' is the record's own inference. The portal presents the Data Insights figures without stating their scope. The inference is reasonable and appropriately hedged in placement, but it is asserted as fact rather than flagged; source_caveats would be the conforming home for that judgment.

The value is a statement about what the release record does not identify ('no IRB or ethics committee is identified in the release record') rather than a name of an ethics review board. This is a value recording the absence of the information the field asks for; the schema-conforming response is to omit the key, since involves_human_subjects: false already carries the substantive fact and the named contacts appear under ethical_reviews.

The notes state 'a Data Access Committee will supervise ethical matters related to dataset distribution and potential dual licensing for commercial use; that is stated there as a planned arrangement.' The plan is correctly marked as a plan and attributed to the preprint, so this does not misstate current state, but a forward-looking arrangement in a governance slot risks being read as the operative process; the disclosure clause is what keeps it conforming.

summary: The full record is substantially well grounded: identifiers, checksums, file inventory, license, governance contacts, limitations, biases and creator roster all trace to attested passages in the declared bundle, and the record consistently prefers the higher-ranked June 2026 Dataverse release over the superseded October 2025 release and the tier-5 historical releases. Source conflicts that matter — the portal's 'Released on: June 17, 2025' against the Dataverse 2026-06-17 publication date, the July 2026 file dates postdating the version publication, the carried-forward (2025-06-30) description stamp, the changed IF archive checksums against unchanged archive names — are disclosed in source_caveats rather than silently resolved, and derived or laboratory-attributed values (data_collectors modality assignments, preprocessing inference, IP restrictions from the preprint) carry their own caveats. No high or medium findings: no unsupported factual claim, no enum violation, no prose-for-list shape error, no commentary embedded in a name or identifier, no fabricated external identifier, and no plan or superseded-release fact presented as the referent's current state. Six low findings remain, all narrow: two sampling_strategies entries lean on project-level portal figures and an is_sample boolean that is interpretive rather than stated; one ethical_reviews contact omits an affiliation its structural twin carries and the bundle supports; one notes sentence asserts a scope inference that belongs in source_caveats; one human_subject_research.ethics_review_board value records the absence of the requested information instead of omitting the key; and one data_governance.notes value carries a planned arrangement, correctly labeled but placed in a slot describing operative governance. Recommended repairs: drop human_subject_research.ethics_review_board; add the University of Montreal affiliation to the Ravitsky contact_person; move the project-level-totals scope judgment from notes to source_caveats; and extend the sampling_strategies caveats to note the 523-versus-464 protein-count conflict and the interpretive basis of is_sample: false.
